body.heading: The teacher learns twice
paragraphs: Explaining how to tie a lace, read a word, or fold a paper plane forces the older child to organise what they know — the oldest finding in education is that teaching is the fastest way to learn. But the second lesson is social: how it feels to be responsible for someone smaller’s success.
That feeling, practised early, becomes the adult who trains new colleagues patiently instead of guarding knowledge.

body.heading: Let them teach it their way
paragraphs: Adults hover and correct; resist. The older child’s method may be slower or stranger than yours, but the younger one is learning from someone closer to their own size of world, and the relationship is the real curriculum.
Step in only for safety or cruelty. Everything else — including glorious inefficiency — is the point.

body.heading: Thank the teacher properly
paragraphs: Name what the older child did as real work: “You taught her to do that. That was proper teaching.” Children rise toward the identities we describe for them, and “patient teacher” is a fine identity to hand someone.
Families run on these invisible promotions. Make sure yours get announced.

takeaway: Let older children teach in their own way, intervene only for safety, and thank them like it counts — because it does.
